title: Interval manager — add/insert with your own bookkeeping

aiGuide.intro: An interval set that stays merged as you add — and later remove — ranges. Assistants reach for the LeetCode "sort and merge" function, which is the wrong shape for a live structure.
plan: Ask: half-open or closed? do touching intervals merge? what is reported?
Invariant + structure: sorted map start → end, floor lookup, running total
AI implements Add against your fields → review → run
AI writes a property test against a bitmap
Remove: you describe the split; AI implements; property test again
Follow-ups: Next(point), balanced tree vs SortedList

stages.name: Add, keep merged
stages.yours: Half-open `[start, end)`. Invariant: **sorted, disjoint, never touching** — `[1,3) + [3,5)` merge. Structure: `SortedList<int,int>` start → end, a binary-search floor lookup, and a running `_covered` total.
stages.ai: **Co-generate** Add, then let the AI write a **property test against a bitmap** — the strongest test for this question.
bad: The LeetCode function: sort a list, merge neighbours, return a new list — O(n log n) on every Add. Often with the R4 bug: `[1,10] + [2,3]` becomes `[1,3]`.
Wrong shape: a function, not a structure
No touching rule, no half-open rule
good: Implement Add(start, end) in IntervalSet below. Half-open [start, end); start >= end throws ArgumentException. Keep my SortedList<int,int> (start → end) sorted, disjoint and non-touching: find the interval at or before start with a binary search, then absorb every interval that overlaps or touches. Update _covered as you go. O(log n + intervals absorbed), no re-sort. State your assumptions first. Show only Add and its helper.
stages.reply: Typical defect (verified planted flaw R4): the merged end set to the absorbed interval's end instead of the **max** — a contained interval **shrinks** the cover.
stages.say: "Touching intervals merge because the ranges are half-open. And I test against a bitmap, so I am not trusting my own examples."
stages.say_iv: I will call addInterval with ranges one at a time. Keep them merged, and let me ask how much is covered and whether a point is covered. Choose the data structure yourself.

stages.name: Remove a range
stages.yours: Say the hard case: **a remove can split one interval into two**. For every overlapping interval: take it out, put back the part left of the cut and the part right of it.
stages.ai: **Co-generate**, and re-run the bitmap property test with removes mixed in.
bad: Removes every interval that overlaps the range — never splits. `[1,7)` minus `[3,4)` removes everything.
The split case is not mentioned, so it is missed
good: Implement Remove(start, end): for every interval overlapping [start, end), take it out and put back the part before start and the part after end, if non-empty. Keep _covered right. Collect the pieces first; do not insert while walking the list by index. Keep my fields and Add unchanged. No re-sort. Explain how _covered stays right. Show only Remove.
stages.reply: Typical defect: inserting the right-hand piece while walking forward by index, which **skips the next interval**.
validate: Remove from the middle splits one interval into two
Remove [7,9) from [1,7): touching, so nothing changes
Property test with mixed add/remove matches a bitmap
stages.fix: Collect-then-insert is a few lines → **a narrow follow-up**: "Collect the leftover pieces in a list and add them after the loop."
stages.say: "A remove can split, so I collect the leftover pieces and add them after the walk."
stages.require: Add `Remove(start, end)`. Removing from the middle splits an interval in two.

checklist: Which method, in which class — paste your class
Implement Log in the Logger class below
Every rule in one sentence, the boundary included
Keep my fields; no new public members
The wrong answers you expect, by name
No DateTime, no timers, no ConcurrentDictionary
Ask for assumptions first, or a reason per test
List your assumptions before the code
Keep the reply small enough to review
Show only Log · change only that line

none: You think and write. This is what is scored.
check: Ask it to attack your design or maths — no code.
cogen: Your design, pasted; the AI fills in mechanical code you can verify fast.
tests: Boilerplate you can check: ask for a reason per expected value.
review: A second reader for a named class of bug — "do not rewrite".
